content.text:
So the project is a static site (html type) or vite. To keep it simple and robust, I'll build a plain HTML/CSS/JS project with no dependencies (no package.json) so default-start serves the static root. But for high quality art/graphics, I'd like canvas 2D rendering with procedurally generated high-detail art — no external assets needed (avoids network). That fits RimWorld-like 2D colony sim: top-down tile map, terrain, colonists, work, needs, building, combat, day/night, weather, zoom/pan, mobile touch controls.

Plan:
- Pure vanilla JS ES modules (served statically). Files: index.html, styles.css, src/*.js.
- High-quality graphics: procedural canvas rendering with:
  - Terrain: grass, dirt, sand, water, rock, tilled soil; autotiling edges with bitmasks; detail (grass tufts, flowers, stones, ripples).
  - Objects: trees (multi-layer canopy with shadow), bushes, rocks, mountains.
  - Buildings: walls, doors, floors, furniture, solar panels, batteries, stove, beds, storage, research bench, turrets.
  - Colonists: detailed pixel/vector sprites with limbs, walk animation, facing, carry items, hairstyles, clothes colors, shadows, selection rings, health bars, name labels.
  - Animals (muffalo-like) wandering.
  - Lighting: day/night cycle with overlay, artificial light pools from lamps/torches.
  - Weather: rain particles, snow, fog.
  - Particle system: dust, sparks, blood, smoke, muzzle flashes.
  - UI: RimWorld-like top bar (resources, date, speed controls, weather), colonist bar, bottom inspect panel, build menu with categories, minimap, notifications.
  - Mobile: touch drag pan, pinch zoom, tap select, long-press context, responsive UI, safe-area, big buttons, bottom sheets.

RimWorld likeness: colony sim mechanics—colonists with needs (hunger, rest, mood), jobs (haul, build, cook, mine, chop, hunt, research, doctor), zoning/stockpiles, building blueprints with construction progress, orders (chop/mine/cancel), drafting/combat with shooting, enemies raiding, turrets, health/injuries, day/night, seasons, research, save/load (localStorage).

This is a big build. Let me be ambitious but ensure it actually runs well. I'll design an architecture:

- world.js: map generation, tiles, objects, pathfinding (A*), pawns, items.
- render.js: layered canvas with cached terrain in offscreen canvases per chunk for performance, dynamic objects drawn each frame sorted by y.
- ui.js: DOM-based UI with CSS, build menus, inspector.
- ai.js/jobs.js: job system.
- main.js: game loop, input.

Given mobile performance, keep map 64x64, chunked terrain caches, requestAnimationFrame with delta, object culling.

Let me think about visual quality. Procedural drawing can look great if done carefully:
- Color palette: RimWorld-ish muted earthy greens and browns, warm lighting.
- Use noise for terrain variation (value noise with seeded PRNG), texture speckles, decals.
- Shadows: soft translucent ellipses.
- Trees: layered circles with irregular edges and darker underside, highlight from light direction.
- Water: animated shimmering with sine waves, shoreline foam.
- Walls: top-down with thick 3D-ish edge on south side, beveled.
- Buildings draw with detail: roof tiles, crates, etc.
- Colonists: 2D "paper doll" top-down-ish three-quarter view RimWorld style, actually RimWorld is top-down with sprites seen slightly from front. I'll draw characters as seen from above-ish front: head circle, body, arms, legs animating, facing direction affects head and body. Use smooth interpolation. Scale ~ 16px tall at zoom 1? I'll design tiles 32px and people ~36px tall.

Let's target tile size 32 at zoom 1, camera with smooth zoom 0.5–3.

Performance: map 80x80 = 6400 tiles; chunk cache 8x8 tiles = 64 chunks of 256x256 px each. Draw visible chunks. Dynamic objects per frame only visible ones, sorted.

Pathfinding A* on grid including walls/doors; moving around objects passability. Need to keep simple but believable.

Job system: colonists autonomously pick work based on priorities:
- Hungry -> eat (from food storage or meal item)
- Tired -> sleep in bed
- Idle -> haul items to stockpile, chop trees, mine rocks, build blueprints, farm, cook at stove, research, patrol/draft.
- Deliver resources to blueprints.

Items: wood, stone, steel, food, meals, silver. Trees drop wood; rocks drop stone/steel.

Raiders: spawn at edge, move to colony, shoot colonists / attack buildings. Drafted colonists auto-fire within range. Turrets fire.

Health: body parts? Keep simplified: health points, injuries affecting moving, bleeding. Doctor tends. Maybe enough.

Mood: from needs and environment; mental break warning.

UI: top bar with resources (wood, stone, steel, food, silver), colony name, date/time clock with day/night arc, weather icon, speed buttons (pause, 1x, 2x, 3x), menu. Left: colonist portraits bar (like RimWorld's colonist bar at top). Bottom-left: inspect panel when selected. Bottom: build toolbar (architect) with categories. Mobile: collapsible; big icons.

Also tutorial hints, help overlay, settings (music? no audio maybe simple WebAudio ambient and SFX generated). "Good animations" — day/night, trees sway, water ripple, characters walking, construction, particles. Sound would be a plus; generate with WebAudio (no assets). Optional mute.

Controls:
- Desktop: WASD/arrow pan, wheel zoom, middle-drag pan, left click select, right click order (move/attack/chop?), space pause, 1/2/3 speeds, Esc cancel, B build, keys.
- Mobile: one-finger drag pan (or in "select mode"?). RimWorld mobile uses drag to pan and tap to select. Pinch zoom. Long press for orders? We'll implement: tap = select, drag = pan, pinch = zoom, two-finger tap = pause? Buttons for orders: when pawn selected, an action bar appears with Move/Attack/Chop/Mine/Deconstruct buttons; then tap target. Building: choose building then drag place.

Need to ensure it works in capture: auto screenshot after 1s. Add attract state? We want the initial screen to look great immediately: game starts with a generated colony with pre-built structures, colonists working, day around morning. No start menu—straight into a polished scene, with a brief "welcome" tip toast. That guarantees screenshot looks great.

Let me plan the code files:

- index.html — canvas + UI structure.
- css/style.css — pretty UI, fonts (system + Google font? offline maybe no network; use system font stack with letter-spacing; could embed a font? Keep system).
- js/main.js — bootstrap, loop.
- js/util.js — RNG, noise, math, color helpers.
- js/world.js — map gen, tiles, defs, objects, items, regions.
- js/path.js — A* + flow.
- js/pawns.js — colonist/animal/raider logic, needs, jobs, health, animation state.
- js/jobs.js — job assignment.
- js/combat.js — attacks/projectiles.
- js/render.js — terrain cache, sprites, lighting, weather, particles.
- js/ui.js — DOM UI, menus, inspector, notifications, minimap.
- js/audio.js — WebAudio ambient/sfx.
- js/save.js — localStorage save/load (maybe).
- js/input.js — pointer/keyboard.

That's a lot, but doable. I need to be careful with correctness—no syntax errors; test in browser with Playwright screenshots. I'll iterate.

Let me think about coordinate and entity model.

Map:
```js
const MAP_W=72, MAP_H=72, TILE=32;
tiles Uint8Array terrain types (grass, dirt, sand, water, rock, floor? floors as objects/terrain).
```
Terrain types: grass(0), dirt(1), sand(2), water(3), rock(4), gravel(5), floor(6), soil(7), marsh(8), snow? Weather changes.

Tile properties: walkable (water no, rock no until mined), fertility, beauty.

Objects: things occupying tiles with footprint (walls 1x1, bed 1x2, stove 1x2, table 3x2, solar 3x3?). Implement generic objects:
```
{id, def, x, y, w, h, rot, hp, maxHp, buildProgress, built, workLeft, resources, jobs...}
```
Defs: wall, door, bed, table, chair, stove, research bench, stockpile (zone), growing zone, lamp, torch, solar panel, battery, turret, sandbag, stone wall, wooden floor (terrain overlay?).

For simplicity, buildings occupy grid; walls block movement; doors passable when open. Blueprints: built=false with workLeft.

Stockpiles/zones: tile-based overlays not objects? Use zones arrays with rects, drawn translucent with labels. Items can be hauled to stockpile tiles.

Items: on ground with type, qty, x,y (float). Render as little piles with icons. Hauling job carries to stockpile.

Pawns:
```
{id, name, kind:'colonist'|'raider'|'animal', x,y (pixel float center), vx,vy, path[], facing, state:'idle'|'walk'|'work'|'eat'|'sleep'|'attack'|'downed', job, needs:{food,rest,joy}, mood, hp, injuries[], carry, clothing colors, skin, hair, weapon}
```
Movement speed ~2.4 tiles/s (76 px/s). Use path waypoints in tile centers. Smooth turning.

Job system: each second or when idle, find job:
Priority: sleep if rest<25 (go bed), eat if food<30 (find meal or raw food in stockpile/near), then assigned work from work priorities (construction, mining, chopping, hauling, cooking, research, farming, cleaning). Use simple job objects {type, target, reservedBy}.

To keep implementation manageable, I'll implement:
- Construction: find blueprint job, colonist walks adjacent, works workLeft/progress with animation (hammer particles), then completes (built=true, consume resources).
- Mining: designated rock tiles (mine designations). Walk adjacent, work, tile becomes gravel, drops stone/steel items.
- Chopping: designated trees. Work, tree falls (animation), drops wood.
- Harvesting crops: growing zones with crops that grow over time; when mature, colonist harvests food.
- Hauling: items not in stockpile and stockpile has space and qty; carry to stockpile.
- Cooking: stove bills: convert raw food (say "agave" or rice) to meals. Simplify: raw food item 'food' (rice), meals item. Colonist cooks at stove: consume 4 food, produce 2 meals. Food need eats meal. Hmm, two food types: "food" raw, "meals" prepared. Top bar shows "Food" total (meals*? ). Keep: raw "grain" + "meal".
- Research: research bench, select tech (auto first tech), progress unlocks turrets maybe.
- Doctor: if injured pawn, tend (bandage) with medicine? Simplify: tend injury reduces bleed.
- Firefight? skip fire hazards maybe rain. Could add fire from raids? Skip.
- Cleaning: filth from dirt/blood; colonist cleans. Maybe skip cleaning jobs but render blood decals that fade.
- Animals: wander, tamed muffalo produce... not needed. Hunt designation by player: drafted pawn hunt? Add hunting job: if player marks animal with hunt, pawn with gun goes and shoots.

Combat:
- Draft mode: select colonist(s), press Draft button, click/tap target to attack or move. In draft, they hold weapon and auto-fire at enemies in range. Raiders spawn in raids (every 2-3 days or button "Raid" for fun?). They path to colony, attack nearest colonist or building. Colonists not drafted flee? Auto-defense: drafted needed. To keep game engaging, add "Defend" auto-draft when raid. Maybe auto: colonists with weapons auto-fire if enemy within 8 tiles.
- Turrets auto-fire.
- Bullets as projectiles with trails; hit chance; damage; blood particles; downed state; death.

Time: game clock starting day 1, 06:00. 1 in-game hour = 8 real seconds at 1x? RimWorld 1 day ~ 16 min at 1x. For demo, day length 3 min at 1x? Let's do 120 sec/day at 1x, so 5 s/hour. Speed 1/2/3 multiply.

Day/night lighting: tint overlay with color from hour; lamps cut light circles (use radial gradients with 'lighter' composite on light layer, then darkness overlay? Technique: draw terrain, then darkness overlay with holes via destination-out of light gradients on a separate offscreen light canvas, then draw over with 'multiply'? Simpler: create light canvas filled with night color; use 'destination-out' radial gradients for light sources; draw over scene with globalAlpha based on darkness. For warm pools, draw additive radial gradients after.)

Weather: clear, rain, fog, snow? Rain particles and darker tint, puddles. Fog overlay drifting. Randomly change.

Graphics detail plan:

Terrain generation:
- Use fBm noise to define biomes: large patches of grass variations, dirt paths, sand near water, rocky area on east side (mountain), a river/lake at south-east? For colony aesthetics: temperate forest with a small pond, rocky ridge to NW.
- Draw each tile with base color + noise stipple (deterministic per tile), grass blades, flowers, pebbles, dirt speckles.
- Autotile edges between terrain types using 4-bit/8-bit masks: blend/dither edges. For sand/dirt/soil edges, draw irregular blobs. Water edge with darker wet sand + foam.
- Pre-render chunks to offscreen canvas with dpr? At zoom up to 2.5, scale cache. Render at 32px per tile at zoom 1; at high zoom will blur; acceptable with crisp sprites? Better render terrain cache at 2x resolution (64px/tile) then draw scaled down; memory: 64 chunks * 512x512*4 = 64MB? too much. Map 72x72 at 2x = 9216^2 px = huge. Chunk 8x8 at 64px/tile = 512x512 => 1MB each, 81 chunks = 84MB. Too much mobile. Use 1x cache (256x256/chunk, 21MB) and draw with smoothing; add dynamic detail on top (grass tufts) drawn per frame? Hmm.

Alternative: draw terrain per frame with simple pattern? 72x72 visible maybe 30x20=600 tiles at zoom 1; each tile with a few ops is fine (~couple thousand draws). At zoomed out full map 72x72=5184 tiles, still ok at 60fps? Canvas 2D can handle ~5000 small rects per frame but with detail ops it may drop. Use culling and level-of-detail: when zoom<0.7, draw simplified flat colors from tiny cache. Use chunk cache at 1x for terrain base (with texture), plus dynamic details culled at low zoom. 21MB memory is okay-ish but mobile maybe. Map 64x64, chunk 8 => 64 chunks * 256KB = 16MB. Acceptable.

Actually can reduce: cache at 24 px/tile? Draw scale. Let's do tile=32 world units, cache resolution 32. Fine.

Trees/objects drawn dynamically for sway and shadows. Number of trees maybe 200; cull visible.

Lighting: overlay canvas at screen resolution, redraw each frame; okay.

Post effects: vignette, subtle bloom? Use canvas filter blur? Expensive. Avoid.

UI design: RimWorld-ish but modern polished:
- Top bar: dark translucent parchment? RimWorld has grey panels. I'll do a sleek dark slate UI with warm amber accents, subtle borders and shadows, rounded 10px, backdrop blur. Icons drawn via inline SVG.
- Left top: colonist bar with round portrait avatars (procedural faces drawn on canvas? Simpler: CSS circular avatar with generated mini canvas portraits). I can draw portraits into small canvases for each colonist. Cute detail. Add name on hover, health bar, mood.
- Top center: date/time + weather icon.
- Top right: resources with icons, speed controls.
- Bottom: build menu with categories; collapsible on mobile.
- Right: notifications stack.
- Inspector panel bottom-left when selecting colonist/building: portrait, name, needs bars, mood, health, inventory, current job; buttons (Draft, Prioritize, etc.).
- Minimap bottom-right (canvas) with viewport rect; tap to jump. On mobile hide or small.
- Tutorial overlay first launch with controls; dismiss. In screenshot, maybe show a subtle "Welcome to..." toast. Ensure not blocking view.

Mobile controls: floating joystick? For RimWorld-like, panning by drag is natural. Add explicit buttons bottom-right for zoom +/-, pause/speed; and a "select/move" mode. Implement touch:
- 1 finger drag on world: if start on pawn -> could select on tap; dragging pans always. Tap (no move > 8px) selects entity or tile. When a pawn is selected and an "order mode" active (move/attack/chop), tap places order. Building mode: drag to place footprint.
- 2 finger pinch zoom.
- Long press (500ms) = context action on target? Could open radial menu; maybe skip, use action buttons.

I'll add an on-screen "command bar" when selection: buttons for Move, Attack, Chop, Mine, Deconstruct, Cancel, Draft; on desktop these are right-click context automatically (right click on tree with pawn selected = chop; on ground = move; on enemy = attack; on object = deconstruct if built, or haul?).

Player designations: In RimWorld you designate trees to chop and rocks to mine via orders. I'll implement "Orders" mode in build toolbar: Chop trees (drag paint), Mine, Deconstruct, Harvest, Hunt. Then colonists automatically do those jobs. That's authentic and gives player agency. Toolbar categories: Orders, Structure, Furniture, Production, Power, Security, Zones.

Zones: stockpile, growing. Drag rectangle; stockpile auto accepts all; growing zone auto plants rice, colonists plant/harvest.

This is getting big but let's do it. Need to manage token budget—I'll write files with substantial but efficient code. Aim for ~4000-5000 lines total maybe too much. Let's aim ~3000 lines across files with dense but readable code. I have a large budget (128k tokens). Let's be systematic and test frequently.

First, set up skeleton and utility, then world, then render, then pawns/jobs, then UI/input, then polish/test.

Let me decide entity/drawing specifics.

World data:
```js
export const TILE=32, MAP_W=64, MAP_H=64;
terrain: Uint8Array (type id)
terrainDefs = [{id:'grass', color..., walk:true, ...}]
Objects: array + grid index (objectAt map). Each object {id, type, x,y,w,h, ...def props, hp, built, workLeft}
```
Walls block tiles. Doors: passable when no enemy; colonists open. For pathfinding, doors walkable.

Trees are objects type 'tree' with 1x1 footprint, block movement; mine rocks 'rock' block; 'bush' walkable? no, blocks but cheap to remove? Trees choppable.

Growing zones: array of {x,y,w,h,type:'grow'}; crops as objects with growth 0..1, plant/harvest. Simpler: crops in tiles array cropGrowth Float32Array; rendered as sprouts/plants; planting job and harvest job.

Stockpiles: zones; items stack; rendering item piles.

Designations: sets of tile keys for chop/mine/deconstruct/harvest/hunt. For deconstruct/build orders on objects by id.

Items: array {id, type, qty, x, y (tile floats), reserved}. Render clusters. Haul: pick up -> carry to stockpile tile.

Terrain resources: rock tiles? I planned rock as objects to display nice boulders, but mountain-ish terrain can be 'stone' walls. Simpler: map has stone cluster areas where each tile is a 'rock' object (boulder) with hp and yields stone; walkable false. Mining designation transforms to gravel terrain and drops stone.

Map gen approach:
- fBm noise for elevation and moisture.
- Pond: circular-ish lake at (48,46) radius 7 using noise edge.
- Mountain/rock field: NW region x<16,y<18 with rock boulders scattered in clusters. Also scattered boulders.
- Colony area center ~ (30,28): flatten to dirt/gravel, pre-built structures:
  - A wooden house 10x8 with walls and door, wooden floor inside, beds (3 singles 1x2), table + chairs, stove, storage crates? 
  - Outside: stockpile zone with items piles (wood, stone, steel, food, meals, silver), solar panels, battery, lamp posts, research bench under roof? Keep partial roof? Skip roofs (top-down without roofs to see inside), draw walls low so interior visible. RimWorld shows interiors with roofs removed view.
  - A field growing rice to the east.
  - Sandbags/turret near south entrance.
- Trees scattered with density from noise, avoid colony.
- Bushes, flowers, rocks, grass detail.
- Colonists 4-6: names, colors. Two inside/around. Their initial jobs set.
- Animals: muffalo x3 grazing, boomrat? Maybe "muffalo" (big furry bison) and "chicken"? Draw 2 animal species.
- Items in stockpile.

Should the game start with buildings complete? Yes, to look established and immediately impressive. Player can expand, raid events after some minutes.

Rendering details:

Tile size 32. Camera {x,y,zoom}. Canvas full screen with dpr cap 2.

Screen transform: worldToScreen. Camera centered.

Terrain chunk cache: For each chunk of 8x8 tiles, render on canvas 256x256 with:
- base fill color per tile with per-tile variation.
- Edge blending: for each tile, examine neighbors of different terrain; draw overlapping fringe using deterministic blob pattern. Implement simple: draw base tile full, then for each neighbor of different type, if neighbor has "higher priority" (e.g., dirt over grass, sand over grass?), draw wavy edge strip. Could be complex. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a high-quality 2D colony-sim game closely modeled on RimWorld, with great graphics, animations, movement, controls, and full mobile support.
- User insists it must be "just like Rimworld" — authentic colony simulation, not merely a visual imitation.

## Requirements
- High-quality, high-detail graphics and animation.
- Good movement and controls, desktop and mobile (touch).
- RimWorld-like systems: colonists, needs, work priorities, building, zones, orders, combat, research, day/night, weather, events.
- Must be playable in browser and work on mobile viewports.
- Workspace was essentially empty at start; build from scratch.

## Decisions
- Pure vanilla HTML/CSS/ES-module JavaScript; no framework/dependencies so the default static server works.
- Canvas 2D rendering with procedurally generated art (no external image assets).
- Map 64×64 tiles at 32 px, terrain pre-rendered once to a 2048×2048 offscreen canvas with detail; y-sorted sprite drawing.
- One in-game day = 3 real minutes at 1×; starts Day 1, 08:15, clear weather, colony “Emberfield”.
- Pre-built starting colony with 6 named colonists staged mid-task for an attractive first screenshot.
- RimWorld-like UI planned: dark charcoal/glass panels, warm gold accents, top bar, colonist portraits, build categories, needs/inspector, notifications, speed controls, help.
- Mobile: drag to pan, pinch zoom, tap to select; two-finger pan while a tool is active; large touch buttons; responsive bottom sheets.
- Simulation systems implemented: needs, mood/mental breaks, skills, traits, work priorities, hauling, cooking, crops, mining/chopping, deconstruction, construction blueprints, sleep/eating at tables, doctor tending, drafting, auto-defense, raids, turrets, research techs, cargo pods, wanderer join, eclipse, weather.

## Work State
### Completed
- `src/util.js`: RNG, noise, colors, easing, min-heap, formatting.
- `src/defs.js`: constants, terrain, buildings, items, techs, traits, names, weapons, animals, seasons.
- `src/world.js`: map access, objects/items/zones, A* pathfinding, time/weather, events, raids, research, particles, combat/projectiles, job-finding, wealth, `coverAt`, `placeNature`, `spawnColonist`.
- `src/gen.js`: procedural terrain (lake, ridge, paths), pre-built house and furniture, solar/battery/turret/sandbags/campfire, stockpile + growing zones, nature scatter, starting items/colonists/animals/jobs.
- `src/pawns.js`: constructor, traits/skills/needs/mood, task system (build/deconstruct/chop/mine/harvest/plant/cook/research/tend/eat/sleep/haul), movement, combat AI, raider AI, animal AI.
- `src/render.js`: camera, screen/world transforms, terrain palette and cached terrain painting with organic edges/details, water/decals/zones/crops/designations/paths/projectiles/particles/floaters/cloud shadows, object ghost and selection outline, full nature/building/item art.
- Verified `new World()` initializes: 13 pawns, 334 objects, 20 items, 2 zones; 20 ticks run without error; all six colonists have staged tasks.

### Active
- `src/render.js` still needs: pawn art (standing/walking/working/sleeping/downed/dead), animals, lighting overlay, weather, ambient (birds/fireflies), post/vignette, screen-space labels, marquee, minimap drawing, build-menu icons, and portrait rendering.
- `src/ui.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/main.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css` are not yet written.
- `world.canPlaceAt(defId,x,y,rot)` is referenced by renderer but not yet implemented.
- Screen-space sorting issue: sleeping pawn under 1×2 bed may need bed sort offset.

### Blocked
- Nothing external; no server started yet, no screenshots taken, no browser validation yet.

## Next Move
1. Finish renderer effects: `drawLighting`, `drawWeather`, `drawAmbient`, `drawPost`, `drawScreenLabels`, `drawMarquee`, `drawMinimap`, `drawPawnWorld`, `drawItem` integration, `drawDefIcon`, `drawPortrait`, `drawBuildingArt` completeness verified.
2. Add `canPlaceAt` and adjust bed y-sort; test rendering in browser.
3. Create `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/ui.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/main.js` with full RimWorld-like UI and touch controls.
4. Start server in tmux (`./start.sh`, static HTML project) and screenshot desktop + mobile via `playwright-cli`/`capture.sh`; inspect images and iterate on visuals and errors.
5. Validate gameplay flows: selection, build placement/costs, orders, zoning, drafting, raids, research, mobile gestures.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/render.js`: largest pending file; art done, effects/pawns/UI labels/icons/minimap pending.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: core simulation; add `canPlaceAt`; verify method gaps.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/pawns.js`: colonist/raider/animal AI and task execution.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/gen.js`: map and starting colony layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/defs.js`: all game data and balance.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/util.js`: shared helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: serves static root via runtime default server.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`: Playwright capture helper expecting `CAPTURE_URL` and `CAPTURE_DIR`.

## Important Context
- Do not use an external image/font network dependency; scene must render offline.
- `TERRAIN_BY_ID` is the indexed terrain array; `TERRAIN` is keyed by name — use `TERRAIN_BY_ID[id]`.
- `T` holds numeric terrain ids (`woodfloor`, `stonefloor`, etc.).

- First raid is scheduled at `absHours + 12.5`; initial cargo event at +4 hours; the 1-second screenshot window is pre-raid.
- Import order: `world.js` imports `gen.js` and `pawns.js`; `gen.js` imports `pawns.js`; avoid adding cycles.
- Commands used successfully: `node --input-type=module -e "import('./src/world.js').then(...)"` for syntax/runtime smoke tests.

## Objective
- Build a high-quality 2D colony-sim game closely modeled on RimWorld, with excellent graphics, animation, movement, controls, and full mobile support.
- User insists it must be "just like Rimworld" — authentic colony simulation, not just a visual imitation.

## Requirements
- High-detail graphics and animation, playable in a browser.
- Strong movement and controls on desktop and touch/mobile viewports.
- RimWorld-like systems: colonists, needs, work priorities, building, zones, orders, combat, research, day/night, weather, events.
- Must work fully offline with no external image/font/CDN dependencies.

## Decisions
- Pure vanilla HTML/CSS/ES-module JavaScript; no frameworks or dependencies.
- Canvas 2D rendering with procedural art; 64×64 map, 32 px tiles, terrain cached to a 2048×2048 offscreen canvas; y-sorted sprites.
- One in-game day = 3 real minutes at 1×; starts Day 1, 08:15, clear weather, colony “Emberfield”.
- Pre-built starting colony with 6 named colonists staged mid-task for an attractive first frame.
- RimWorld-like UI: dark charcoal/glass panels, warm gold accents, top bar, colonist portraits, build categories, inspector, notifications, speed controls, help, minimap.
- Mobile: drag to pan, pinch zoom, tap to select, large touch targets, responsive bottom sheets.
- Procedural Web Audio sound engine; no audio assets.
- Resources are consumed when a blueprint is placed; blueprints built by colonist construction work.

## Work State
### Completed
- `src/util.js`: RNG, noise, color helpers, formatting, min-heap.
- `src/defs.js`: terrain, buildings, items, techs, traits, names, weapons, animals, seasons, work types; includes `TERRAIN_BY_ID`.
- `src/world.js`: map access, objects/items/zones, A* pathfinding, time/weather/events/raids, research, particles, combat, job-finding, wealth, `coverAt`, `canPlaceAt`, `canAfford`/`missingFor`/`spend`, `queueBuild`, `cancelBuild`, `designate`, `designateHunt`, `clearDesignations`.
- `src/gen.js`: procedural terrain, lake/ridge/paths, pre-built house/furniture, solar/battery/turret/sandbags/campfire, stockpile/grow zones, nature, items, six colonists with staged tasks, animals.
- `src/pawns.js`: needs/mood/mental breaks, skills, traits, priorities, full task system (build/deconstruct/chop/mine/harvest/plant/cook/research/tend/eat/sleep/haul), movement, combat/raider/animal AI.
- `src/render.js`: cached terrain with organic edges/details, water/decals/zones/crops/designations/paths, projectiles/particles/floaters/clouds, objects/nature/buildings/items art, blueprint + build ghost, pawn human/animal art (walking/working/sleeping/downed/dead, hair, hats, glasses, weapons, carried items, health bars, selection brackets), lighting/weather/ambient birds + fireflies/vignette, screen labels, marquee, minimap, building icons, portraits.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized click/build/chop/mine/gunshot/turret/melee/death/chime/research/alarm/thunder/crash/collapse/cook/tend/eclipse sounds; ambience and rain loop; mute.
- `package` of UI: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/ui.js` written (top bar, resources, portraits, inspector, architect menu, work/research/log/menu sheets, help, notifications, alerts, game-over).
- Smoke-tested world creation, 20 ticks, 600 ticks, build placement, and `canPlaceAt` via Node; all passed.
- `src/render.js` syntax verified with `node --check`.

### Active
- `src/input.js` not yet written: pointer/mouse/touch controls, tools, selection, marquee, pan/zoom, keyboard shortcuts, minimap/portrait interactions wiring.
- `src/main.js` not yet written: bootstrapping, animation loop, world/render/ui/input wiring, loading fade.
- `ui.js` needs runtime/browser validation; no screenshots or console-error checks yet.
- `window.hasTech` calls in UI? (UI uses `this.world.hasTech`, ok); confirm all cross-module method/property references at runtime.
- `renderer.dpr` access in UI menu is valid; `renderer.weatherOff` toggle is referenced but not yet honored by renderer.

### Blocked
- Nothing external; no server or browser validation started yet.

## Next Move
1. Write `src/input.js` with mouse + touch handling: tap select, drag pan, pinch zoom, marquee selection, tool painting/placement, right-click or long-press context orders, keyboard (WASD/arrows, 1–3, Space, R, Esc, H).
2. Write `src/main.js`: instantiate `World`, `Renderer`, `AudioEngine`, `UI`, `Input`; wire `ui.input`, RAF loop (dt cap), initial loading fade; start audio on first gesture.
3. Add renderer support for `weatherOff`; verify UI/build menu calls (`setTool`, `rotateTool`, `cancelTool`, `selectPawn`, `focus`) all exist.
4. Start static server via `./start.sh` and screenshot desktop + mobile with Playwright (`capture.sh`/`PLAYWRIGHT`), check console errors, inspect visuals.
5. Fix any visual/UX/runtime defects; validate selection, build placement/costs, orders, zoning, drafting, raids, research, mobile gestures.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/render.js`: rendering pipeline, pawn art, lighting/weather, minimap/portraits/icons; `draw` calls `this.hover`, `hoverPawn`, `hoverObj`, `selected`, `selectedObj`, `tool`, `zonePreview`, `marquee`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: simulation APIs used by UI/input; recent additions at `canPlaceAt`/`queueBuild`/`designate`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: new UI layer; expects `this.input` with `setTool`, `rotateTool`, `cancelTool`, and will call `renderer.focus`, `drawMinimap`, `drawPortrait`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/pawns.js`: pawn state/fields used by renderer/UI (`mood`, `activity()`, `task`, `needs`, `appearance`, `facing`, `walkPhase`, `workAnim`, `carry`, `seatId`).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/defs.js`: all ids/balance used across modules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: `AudioEngine.play(name, opts)`, `setMuted`, `resume`, `setRain`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM ids/classes referenced by `ui.js`; loads `src/main.js`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: full UI styling including mobile breakpoints and sheets.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/gen.js`: starting layout/colonists; map and initial job staging.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/util.js`: helpers used everywhere (`hash2`, `shade`, `roundRect`, `timeString`, `dayStamp`).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: static server launcher.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`: Playwright capture helper expecting `CAPTURE_URL` and `CAPTURE_DIR`.

## Important Context
- No external image/font/audio/network assets are allowed; everything must render/sound offline.
- `TERRAIN_BY_ID` is the indexed array; `TERRAIN` is keyed by name. `T` holds numeric ids.
- Beds are intentionally non-blocking; `canPlaceAt` disallows floors under existing objects and supports same-type blueprints.
- `world.update` handles pause/speed; `ui.setSpeed` sets `world.paused`/`world.speed`.
- `renderer.selected` is a `Set` of pawn ids; `selectedObj`/`selectedZone` are object/zone ids; `hover` is world coords; `tool` shape: `{kind:'build',defId,rot}`, `{kind:'order',order}`, `{kind:'zone',zone}`, `{kind:'zoneRemove'}`.
- `renderer.draw()` now stores `this.dt`; ambient uses it. Dead colonists render for 90 real seconds (`animTime - deadAt`).
- `UI` relies on event delegation and DOM ids in `index.html`; `ui.input` must be assigned after `Input` construction.
- World events: `notice`, `colonists`, `tech`, `raid`, `raidEnd`, `gameover`; UI subscribes.
- First raid scheduled ~12.5 in-game hours after start; initial cargo event at +4 hours.
- Successful smoke command pattern: `node --input-type=module -e "import('./src/world.js').then(...)"`.
- Files remain uncommitted in the git working tree; no server/screenshots taken yet.

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a high-quality 2D colony-sim game closely modeled on RimWorld, with excellent graphics, animation, movement, controls, and full mobile support.
- User insists it must be "just like Rimworld" — authentic colony simulation, not just a visual imitation.

## Requirements
- High-detail graphics and animation, playable in a browser.
- Strong movement and controls on desktop and touch/mobile viewports.
- RimWorld-like systems: colonists, needs, work priorities, building, zones, orders, combat, research, day/night, weather, events.
- Must work fully offline with no external image/font/CDN dependencies.

## Decisions
- Pure vanilla HTML/CSS/ES-module JavaScript; no frameworks or dependencies.
- Canvas 2D rendering with procedural art; 64×64 map, 32 px tiles, terrain cached to a 2048×2048 offscreen canvas; y-sorted sprites.
- One in-game day = 3 real minutes at 1×; starts Day 1 at 08:15 (`START_HOUR = 8.25`), clear weather, colony “Emberfield”.
- Pre-built starting colony with 6 named colonists staged mid-task for an attractive first frame.
- RimWorld-like UI: dark charcoal/glass panels, warm gold accents, top bar, colonist portraits, build categories, inspector, notifications, speed controls, help, minimap.
- Desktop: left click selects/marquees; right/middle drag pans; right click orders/cancels; wheel zoom; WASD/arrows, Space, 1–3, R, Esc, H, M, F, B shortcuts.
- Touch: tap selects; one-finger drag pans when no tool; with a tool active one finger paints and two fingers pan/pinch-zoom; double-tap focuses.
- Resources are consumed when a blueprint is placed; blueprints built by colonist construction work.
- Simulation runs on fixed 1/30 s steps decoupled from render frame rate so slow machines do not slow the in-game clock.
- Adaptive optimizations: lighting pass skipped in daylight, half-resolution light canvas, baked vignette overlay (no per-frame soft-light), weather toggle supported via `renderer.weatherOff`.
- Architect panel opens by default on desktop; item cards are vertical icon/name/cost tiles.

## Work State
### Completed
- `src/util.js`, `src/defs.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/gen.js`, `src/pawns.js`, `src/render.js`, `src/audio.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/ui.js` implemented.
- `src/input.js` implemented: pointer/touch pan, pinch zoom, tap select, marquee selection, tool painting (build/orders/zones), right-click move/attack/cancel, hunt, zone removal, keyboard shortcuts.
- `src/main.js` implemented: bootstraps World/Renderer/AudioEngine/UI/Input, fixed-step simulation loop, loading fade, resize/orientation handling, first-gesture audio resume, error overlay.
- UI/input wiring validated in browser: architect opens by default with 5 structure cards; clicking wall card sets tool; clicking map places a blueprint and deducts wood (172 → 167).
- Fixed favicon 404 by adding inline SVG data URI.
- Fixed start time to show 08:15.
- Fixed build card icons (`drawDefIcon` now scales 2×) and redesigned cards; stone items appear dim because they are tech-locked.
- Moved notifications above minimap and tool hint to bottom-right free zone so they no longer cover each other.
- Throttled duplicate notices in `UI.showNotice` (e.g., repeated wall placement updates one card).
- Syntax checks pass for all `src/*.js`.
- Server running in tmux session `ember` at `http://localhost:3000` (HTTP 200).
- Playwright browser installed and working; screenshots captured: `screenshots/desktop-1.png`, `screenshots/zoom-house.png`, `screenshots/desktop-2.png`, `screenshots/build-tool.png`.

### Active
- Browser validation continues: inspector/portrait selection, work/research/log/menu sheets, orders, zoning, drafting, raids, research, mobile gestures/layout.
- Performance is poor in this Xvfb/SwiftShader environment (~5 fps full scene, ~11 fps with nearly everything disabled); not yet confirmed whether real GPU browsers are acceptable.
- Visual polish pending: terrain transitions still look blocky/flat; house interior floor/walls monotone; some building art (research bench) reads as a black slab.

### Blocked
- Nothing external; no confirmed runtime errors except favicon (now fixed). Browser console otherwise clean.

## Next Move
1. Reload and validate selection/inspector via portrait click; test draft, work-sheet priority cycling, research card selection, log, menu toggles, and help overlay.
2. Test orders (chop/mine/deconstruct/cancel), zone creation/removal, blueprint cancel/refund, and right-click move/attack.
3. Capture and inspect mobile viewport (e.g., 390×844) and test tap, drag pan, pinch zoom, build painting, architect sheet behavior.
4. Fix visual defects: strengthen wall/floor contrast, add organic terrain edge blending/richer floor detail, improve research bench appearance.
5. Consider a lightweight adaptive quality mode for low-FPS/mobile (skip post/cloud shadows, lower particle counts) and verify frame pacing.
6. Re-check console errors and long-run stability (raids, research completion, deaths/game-over).

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: complete pointer/touch/keyboard control layer.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: boot and fixed-step RAF loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/render.js`: rendering pipeline, lighting/post optimizations, terrain/objects/pawns, icon and portrait drawing.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: top bar, inspector, architect, sheets, notices, alerts, minimap updates.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: simulation APIs, jobs, events, build/zone/designation logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/pawns.js`: pawn needs, tasks, combat, movement AI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/gen.js`: starting map, house/furniture layout, staged colonists.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/defs.js`: terrain/building/item/tech/work definitions; `START_HOUR` changed to 8.25.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: complete desktop/mobile UI styling and recent layout fixes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM structure, favicon data URI, module entry.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural Web Audio effects/ambience.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: captured desktop/build screenshots for visual review.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: static server launcher (port 3000).

## Important Context
- All changes remain uncommitted in the git working tree.
- Server: tmux session `ember` running `./start.sh`; URL `http://localhost:3000`.
- Playwright commands work via `playwright-cli`; use `window.EMBERFIELD` for debugging (`world`, `renderer`, `ui`, `input`, `audio`).
- Full-scene FPS measured ~5 in current Xvfb/SwiftShader setup; blank page rAF ~60; disabling almost all draw calls raises only to ~11 fps, indicating software-canvas raster cost rather than JS logic.
- `world.update` itself internally caps `sdt` at 0.06 s; main loop now calls it repeatedly in 1/30 s fixed steps up to 10 per frame.
- Build stroke logic: 1×1 buildings paint immediately along a Bresenham line; larger footprints place once on pointer-up. Resources are spent per placed blueprint.
- `stop.sh`/killing tmux session `ember` is needed when done testing.
- `renderer.selected` is a `Set` of pawn ids; `selectedObj`/`selectedZone` are ids; `hover` is world coords; `tool` shape `{kind:'build',defId,rot,anchor}`, `{kind:'order',order}`, `{kind:'zone',zone}`, `{kind:'zoneRemove'}`.
- UI expects `input.setTool`, `rotateTool`, `cancelTool`, and `ui.input` assigned after Input construction.
- Removed per-frame `refreshArchitect()` from `UI.update`; architect is refreshed on tool changes to avoid rebuilding icon canvases 5×/s.
